title: His Gibson guitar, playing single, and banjo versus guitar in Dixieland
summary: Verrett discusses his Gibson, solo jobs and pay, and why banjo suits Dixieland better than guitar.

story.theme_name: Banjo, guitar and the rhythm section: instruments and players

blocks.x: Yeah, that's a Gibson. I had this.
I had this guitar. This big one.

You used a fast dominant one. Yeah, I had this, but a pickup went bad on. Pickups, it's got to go through a war line with a pickup. Come on, you see? Yeah, it's a big Gibson. It's gone. It's gone. It's gone. There's no effects. Maybe the microphone probably. Well, I called them. I asked them. I said, I don't know what they said. They want a 16-hour old hard.

I said, I don't know what I want to get it done. I'll be asking for the guitar, see? Most of the time, I used to play single, you know, no electric. A lot of people call me up to play single, you know?
Yeah, it's big enough instruments you've got a good tone out of there without the electric guitar.

Yeah, it's got a good tone, see? Take that tailpiece off. Yeah. I played a lot of singles. Then I played with Noon at the Zipper Trio. So a lot of them tell me there's one of me, so I go up and make more now. I make $50 to $20 now.
I sent sales on a couple of them. He likes them. Yeah, he likes them. Sales is a good musician, good entertainer, too. Good man.
Otherwise, do you like the guitar in the band as well as banjo, or what do you think?

Well, for the Dixieland band, the guitar, banjo would be best. A little guitar is a good instrument all the way around, but I don't know, this, it looks like that planking, it doesn't get planking or fist, you know, Dixieland music. But this is more, piano, you know, so that planking would fit the Dixieland music better than the guitar.
